title: Coq au Vin
subtitle: Slow-braised chicken in red wine with lardons and mushrooms
excerpt: Chicken pieces braised slowly in a full bottle of red wine with lardons, pearl onions, and mushrooms until the sauce is glossy and the meat is falling from the bone. The great French braise.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coq au vin (cockerel in wine) is one of the most celebrated dishes of the French bourgeois kitchen, traditionally made with an old rooster (coq) whose tough, flavourful flesh benefited from long, slow braising in wine. The modern version uses a regular chicken or chicken pieces, which require less time. The dish is documented in French cookbooks from the late nineteenth century but the technique of braising poultry in wine is much older. The wine is the entire braising liquid: a full bottle is used, and a cheap wine makes a cheap sauce. The sauce should be dark, glossy, and deeply flavoured, reduced to a coating consistency at the end. The dish is better made a day ahead: the flavours deepen overnight and the fat can be lifted from the surface when cold.

recipeTools.notes: A large, wide, heavy casserole or saucepan with a lid that fits in the oven.

content.text: Brown the chicken pieces in batches over high heat: crowding the pan causes steaming rather than browning and the dish will lack colour and depth. The chicken must be deeply golden-brown on all sides before any liquid is added. The lardons are rendered first to provide the fat for browning. The sauce is thickened at the end by removing the chicken and reducing the braising liquid vigorously over high heat until it reaches a coating consistency. Return the chicken to the sauce to warm through before serving.

items.preparation: bone-in, skin-on thighs and drumsticks; or a jointed whole chicken

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Render the lardons in a large, heavy casserole over medium heat for 5 minutes. Remove and set aside. Increase the heat to high. Brown the chicken pieces in batches in the lardon fat, adding a little oil as needed, until deeply golden on all sides. Remove each batch and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the shallots and cook for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato puree. Cook for 1 minute. Scatter over the flour and stir to coat everything. Pour in the wine and stock, scraping up any brown bits. Add the thyme, bay, salt, and pepper. Return the chicken and lardons. Bring to a simmer.

Cover and transfer to the oven. Cook for 45 minutes. Meanwhile, fry the mushrooms in butter over high heat until golden. Add the mushrooms to the casserole and cook for a further 20 minutes until the chicken is very tender. Lift the chicken and vegetables into a warm serving dish. Reduce the sauce over high heat until glossy and coating. Pour over the chicken. Scatter with parsley.
